editorial.marketOverview: Friday's shortened session remains the latest cash observation. QQQ rose 2.66% according to Quantisnow versus 2.69% in the repository; SOX gained 4.69% in the repository. External SMH gain of 3.79% differs from the repository implied 4.17%, so exact relative returns are not synchronized. WSJ reports Nasdaq gained 6.7% for the week after a 10% decline the previous week.
editorial.whatChanged: Repository report refreshed to 15:53 ET without a change in score (-7) or quoted equity and rate figures. Open Watch remains updated at 19:48 UTC with no new dated catalyst. Fresh external coverage reinforces the rebound but also notes unresolved AI financing and export risks.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Broad participation and semiconductor strength support neutral rather than bearish bias, but holiday liquidity and elevated rates limit confidence in continuation. Earlier Friday FedWatch pricing favored a December hike; exact latest probabilities, VXN and matched Brent/WTI settlements are not verified. Oil supply risk remains two-sided.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 30 tests the rebound with normal liquidity and weekend oil developments. Tuesday December 1 brings manufacturing PMI, ISM and official JOLTS at 10 ET; Credo earnings remain repository-listed, not issuer-confirmed. Wednesday December 2 ADP at 08:15 ET adds rate sensitivity. Reported Nvidia congressional hearings next week are a watch item without confirmed timing.
editorial.bullCase: A sustained chip-led recovery with broad participation and cooling volatility could extend gains if yields stabilize. The weekly rebound supports this possibility but does not establish a durable trend.
editorial.bearCase: A reversal of semiconductor relative strength, narrowing breadth or renewed oil-driven inflation pressure could unwind the holiday rally. A ten-year yield above 5% would reinforce downside risk; AI financing and export uncertainty remain unresolved.
editorial.watchNext: Monitor weekend OPEC+ developments, Monday futures and cash breadth, paired Treasury yields, fresh VXN/VIX and matched oil contracts. Verify hearing and earnings dates and compare Tuesday and Wednesday releases with consensus.
